title: Gender equity in sport
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches general gender roles and gender identity from a NSW Society and Culture course, while the new point is about inequities in pay, media coverage and coaching in sport, so it is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Gender equity in sport
card: Gender equity means women and men get fair treatment and fair chances in sport. Gaps in some areas show where it is still lacking.
in many sports, women athletes are paid less than men, or have less prize money or fewer contracts.
women's sport often gets less time on TV and less space in news and online. Less coverage can mean fewer fans and fewer sponsors.
fewer women work as coaches, referees, administrators and board members. This means women have less say in how sport is run.
draft.remember: Gaps in pay, media coverage and women's leadership roles show where gender equity is still lacking.

a.q: A sport gives its women's league far less TV time than its men's league. Which gender equity gap does this show?
a.why: TV time is a form of media coverage, so unequal TV time shows a media gap. Pay and coaching are different gaps, and the case says nothing about them.
a.clue: Think about what TV time measures.

b.q: A netball association has mostly women players, but almost all its coaches and board members are men. What does this best show?
opts: A leadership gap, as women have less say in running it
A pay gap, as women players earn less
A media gap, as women's games are not shown
No gap, as most players are women
b.why: The case is about who coaches and sits on the board, so it shows a leadership gap. Many women playing does not mean women have a say in decisions. Pay and media are not mentioned.
b.clue: Ask who makes the decisions, not who plays.

b.best: A leadership gap, as women have less say in running it
